content.comment_body: If I need the clock to retain memory for more than 20 days without power, what is recommended? Should I use a UPS to supply power during outages?
Yes, using a UPS is one possible solution.

Alternatively, you could set up an external clock source. If there's internet access, you can enable network time. Without internet, a device like a Raspberry Pi with a GPS module can serve as a local time server for the [product_name] to get the correct time.
This feature isn't supported on all [product_name] units. Earlier models with certain firmware versions do not have this function.
Using a deep cycle battery combined with solar panels can provide backup power and recharge to the [product_name].

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants are exploring ways to extend memory retention and timekeeping for [product_name] modules beyond the standard 20-day power loss backup. There is some uncertainty about available options and product or firmware compatibility, especially regarding time synchronization and hardware variations. Solutions such as UPS, external network clocks, and solar-powered batteries are suggested, with discussion highlighting usability challenges related to practical implementation and technical knowledge.
analysis.user_expectations: Users are looking for a method to help the clock maintain accurate time for periods far longer than 20 days without mains power, preferring options that are cost-effective, dependable, and require minimal manual upkeep.
